connector: Peter, Edmund and Trumpkin found Caspian just in time. Now the High King is in command, and there is a war still to settle. Today, ask what this story still has to answer, and watch the way Peter chooses to answer it. The way someone settles a fight shows what they value.

a.raw: peter told caspian that he was to wounded to fight miraz in single combat
a.fixed: Peter told Caspian that he was too wounded to fight Miraz in single combat.
a.why: Capitals on Peter, Caspian and Miraz; too (meaning more than enough), not to; a period ends it.

b.raw: edmund carried the challenge and glenstorm and wimbleweather walked beside him
b.fixed: Edmund carried the challenge, and Glenstorm and Wimbleweather walked beside him.
b.why: Capitals on the three names; a comma before the and that starts a new complete thought; a period ends it.

notes.wgrd: Explain how resolution reveals theme: name what the story still has to settle, notice the way the characters choose to settle it, and ask what that way values.
vocab: An invitation to fight or compete that must be answered.
Fighting; single combat is one against one.
To say words aloud for someone else to write down.
An official who oversees a contest and keeps order.
notes.wordParts: Review of the unit’s bases: port, tract, struct, spect, ject, script/scribe, rupt, duct/duce, form, plus press = push, tain = hold, lev = lift.
notes.grammar: Dialogue punctuation: quotation marks fence off the exact words; the comma or end mark goes inside the closing quotation mark; a tag like said Peter joins with a comma.
notes.spelling: Cumulative review: a hard word is often two or three rules stacked up. Take it apart: se + par + ate + ion; forget + t + able.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: The OAO Seven Pillars are honesty, respect, courtesy, responsibility, courage, service and perseverance. In Chapter 13, Peter takes command. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: Caspian is wounded, so Peter will not let him fight. Peter sends Miraz a challenge to single combat with himself, so that two armies won’t have to fight.
items.why: He puts himself in danger to protect everyone else.
items.hint: Who is in danger now, and who is safer?

items.t: The Bear says the bears always had the right to supply one marshal. Peter says, “It is your right. And you shall be one of the marshals.”
items.why: Peter honours an old right, even though Trumpkin warns him the Bear will suck his paws.

items.t: Reepicheep asks to be a marshal. Peter gravely tells him it would not be quite fair to Miraz, since some humans are afraid of mice.
items.why: He says no without laughing at the Mouse.

items.t: Edmund asks if Peter can beat Miraz. Peter says, “That’s what I’m fighting him to find out.”
items.why: He doesn’t pretend to be sure, and he goes anyway.

transcripts.welcome: Hello, it’s Nell. Peter has found Caspian, and the High King is in command. Today’s question: when there is more than one way to settle a fight, what does the way you choose say about you?
transcripts.read: Listen to the challenge letter. It’s full of old, formal words, and every one of them is chosen on purpose. Then watch Peter choose his marshals, and say no to one volunteer. Notice how he says no.
transcripts.morphology: This is a review of every base in the unit. Port, carry. Tract, pull. Struct, build. Spect, look. Ject, throw. Script, write. Rupt, break. Duct, lead. Form, shape. You know a lot of Latin now. Take a long word apart, and it will tell you what it means.
